title: Defense of the Law and the Body of Christ
english: They do these things through fear of falling into punishment, but with desire and longing. For from this it will happen to bear all things soberly and courageously, not only the pleasant things but also the painful and unpleasant ones, and to go toward every diligent task with eagerness.

Since some reproach and belittle me for seeking your testimonies (Ps 118:22), you have removed the reproach and the belittling from me. How could these be removed? For the coming knowledge of the truth of those formerly reproaching and belittling me; and if this exists, they themselves will seek your testimonies.

Another scripture says, 'I have declared your ways' (Ps 118:26), meaning: the ways that lead to you are not other ways of virtues, O Lord; I have declared them practically with diligent intention and in appropriate works, and you heard me; therefore, toward those who obey I say, 'Teach me your statutes' (Ps 118:29).

He who will turn away from the way of unrighteousness and approaching the law of God wants to be perfected and established toward God, who brings the ends of good things (Ps 118:29). For as one having hated ignorance has had a longing for the opposing knowledge, so one who has turned himself from ignorance and approached by faith asks the teacher: 'Turn ignorance away from me and have mercy on me by your knowledge.'

The voice is not one who is conscious of sin, but of one suspecting, as in 'From my secret things cleanse me' (Ps 118:39). But I am confident in what you will remove, the suspected reproach, being convinced of what your judgments are, being full of kindness and love for mankind.

If it is possible to say all things about the spoken word, stand by; for he himself is both mercy and salvation of the Lord (Ps 118:41-42). Therefore, it is necessary for us to seek the mercy of the Lord, the salvation according to his mercy. For having been shown mercy and having been saved...
We answer those who previously reproached us as lacking the mercy and salvation of God (Ps 118:43-44).

I ask for insights, not merely such words; even if I sometimes fall into difficulties regarding providence and similar matters, I do not wish to give an answer that merely resolves the contradictions of those who wander, but rather, since you have opened my mouth with your own goodness, give me an interpretation of the truth through your word, so that the word of truth may not be entirely torn from my mouth, but that I may be able to speak somewhat regarding the unanswerable ones, saying: 'I have erred concerning your judgments, your examined and tested words; how do you judge and provide for men?' (Ps 118:51).

Do not let the word of truth depart vehemently from my mouth. For indeed, keeping your law will not only happen in this age but unto the age, the words of Jesus not passing away. We therefore keep God's law according to the image of things, previously kept by the Jews according to a shadow, to be kept for us according to the future good things unto the age of ages (Ps 118:51).
Regarding the heterodox who boast against the law by slandering it (Ps 118:53), I was intensely occupied with its keeping, and how much I was shaken in my assent to it, not enduring [the slander].

Since of the sinners some sin lawlessly, not even attempting the beginning of laws, and others transgress it while in law, discouragement seized me from the sinners who abandon God's law; for if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; and if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it. And it is fitting to be grieved for our brothers who sin, what kind of people they are, and not to be divided against this holy one (Ps 118:58).
